headline: KSE-100 sheds 1,464 points to 179,847 as Hormuz impasse and hawkish Fed bets rattle risk sentiment
mood: Risk-off · Hormuz standoff and Fed repricing dominate

five_things.html: The KSE-100 shed 1,464 points (−0.81%) to close at 179,846.68 on Tuesday, retreating from an intraday high of 181,017 as automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, fertiliser, E&P and OMC counters came under broad selling pressure amid fading hopes of a US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz (Business Recorder, The Nation).

Washington's new demands on Tehran — including compensation for conflict casualties — have clouded a near-term Strait of Hormuz reopening, keeping tanker traffic constrained and crude bid; Brent settled near $87.72 and WTI near $82.13, both up roughly 5% on the session (CNBC, Al Jazeera).

The US 10-year yield pushed above 4.7%, its firmest since January, as oil-driven inflation risk lifted the market-implied odds of a 25bp September hike to roughly 55% — a sharp reversal from July's dovish-leaning hold (Washington Post, Chase).
Gold pushed back above $4,400/oz and silver rallied to a seven-week high near $65.50/oz as investors sought cover from the Hormuz standoff and firmer rate-hike odds (Kitco, CNBC).

Islamabad is readying for a fifth EFF review mission next month that could unlock roughly $1.2bn (a $1bn EFF tranche plus $200m under the RSF), with energy-sector circular debt, the FY27 budget and privatisation progress under the microscope (ProPakistani).

matrix.local_html: The KSE-100 retreated 0.81% (−1,464 pts) to 179,846.68 on Tuesday after touching an intraday high of 181,017, as broad selling in banks, cement, fertiliser, autos, E&P and OMCs offset last week's rally; market breadth stayed mixed with roughly even gainers and losers (Business Recorder). The SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% at its July 27 review for a second straight pause, even as July CPI cooled to 9.2% y/y from 11.1% (food inflation actually accelerated to 10.6%), keeping real rates restrictive (Trading Economics). Six-month KIBOR continues to track a touch above the policy rate (EST.). The interbank USD/PKR was broadly steady at 277.67, down marginally from 277.70 (SBP). On the IMF front, Islamabad is preparing for a fifth EFF/RSF review mission next month that could release roughly $1.2bn, with energy circular-debt targets and privatisation progress the key sticking points (ProPakistani).
matrix.gcc_html: Seven OPEC+ members — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman — lifted output by a further 188,000 bpd from August, the alliance's fifth straight monthly increase as it continues unwinding voluntary cuts even with Hormuz-linked price risk elevated (Vision2030.ai). Saudi Arabia's non-oil private sector stayed in solid expansion, with the Riyad Bank PMI easing only slightly to 53.1 in July from 53.3 in June as output and new orders kept climbing; Kuwait's reading rebounded over the same stretch (AGBI). The PIF, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, has approved its 2026–2030 strategy, pivoting from rapid asset growth toward value creation with tourism, travel and entertainment as priority sectors under Vision 2030 (Gulf Business).
matrix.global_html: US equities closed lower Tuesday — the S&P 500 fell 0.24%, the Dow slipped 0.16% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.55% — as tech weakness and a stalled US-Iran Hormuz negotiation overshadowed industrial-sector gains (Washington Post). The 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 4.7% — its highest since January — as oil-driven inflation risk pushed market-implied odds of a 25bp September Fed hike to roughly 55%, a marked hawkish reversal from July's 9-3 hold vote (Chase). Brent and WTI both surged roughly 5% to settle near $87.72 and $82.13 respectively, extending a fourth straight advance on fears that a naval blockade will keep the Strait of Hormuz constrained (CNBC). Gold and silver caught a safe-haven bid, with gold back above $4,400/oz and silver at a seven-week high near $65.50/oz (Kitco).

legislative.policy_html: Fifth IMF EFF/RSF review mission due next month — energy circular debt, FY27 budget and privatisation progress under scrutiny for a ~$1.2bn disbursement
legislative.impact_html: Wins: banks and FX reserves if the tranche clears, sovereign risk premium. Loses: energy consumers facing tariff/circular-debt adjustment conditionality, importers if reform slippage pressures the PKR.

legislative.policy_html: OPEC+ raises output 188,000 bpd for August; PIF approves 2026–2030 strategy prioritising tourism and entertainment
legislative.sectors: Energy, Sovereign wealth, Tourism/Entertainment, Oil-importer FX
legislative.impact_html: Wins: oil-importing economies and consumers via incremental supply; Saudi non-oil diversification plays (tourism, leisure, entertainment). Loses: OPEC+ producers' per-barrel fiscal revenue as supply grows into a Hormuz-risk-inflated price.

legislative.policy_html: Markets reprice toward a 25bp September hike (~55% odds) after July's split 9-3 hold, driven by oil-led inflation risk
legislative.sectors: USD, Rates, EM FX (incl. PKR), Equities
legislative.impact_html: Wins: US dollar, fixed-income savers, money-market yields. Loses: rate-sensitive equities, EM currencies including the PKR, and leveraged borrowers facing a higher-for-longer curve.

levels.support_note: first floor; deeper support at 176,500 (desk estimate)
levels.resistance_note: Tuesday's intraday high; then Monday's close of 181,310

desk_stance_html: We read Tuesday's pullback as a geopolitical repricing, not a trend reversal — the KSE-100 gave back barely 0.8% after a strong run, and the drivers (Hormuz impasse, a firmer Fed-hike narrative) are external rather than domestic-earnings-driven. A close back above 181,000 would reopen record territory; a break of 178,500 would point to a deeper retracement toward 176,500. Banks, fertiliser and cement — last week's leaders — are the counters to watch for signs of the dip being bought versus extended. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

KSE-100 sheds 1,464 points as the Hormuz standoff and a hawkish Fed repricing dominate the tape.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
US equities closed lower Tuesday — S&P 500 −0.24%, Dow −0.16%, Nasdaq −0.55% — as tech weakness and stalled US-Iran Strait of Hormuz talks weighed on sentiment. The 10-year Treasury yield pushed above 4.7%, its highest since January, with markets now pricing roughly 55% odds of a 25bp September Fed hike — a sharp reversal from July's split 9-3 hold. Brent and WTI both surged ~5% to settle near $87.72 and $82.13 on fears a naval blockade keeps Hormuz constrained. Gold reclaimed $4,400/oz and silver hit a seven-week high near $65.50 on safe-haven demand.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 retreated 0.81% (−1,464 pts) to 179,846.68, giving back ground after touching an intraday high of 181,017 as banks, cement, fertiliser, autos, E&P and OMCs all came under selling pressure. SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a second straight review even as July CPI cooled to 9.2% from 11.1% (food inflation, notably, accelerated to 10.6%). USD/PKR interbank held broadly steady at 277.67. Islamabad is preparing for a fifth IMF EFF/RSF review mission next month that could unlock roughly $1.2bn, with energy circular debt and privatisation progress the key tests.

GCC
Seven OPEC+ members lifted output by 188,000 bpd for August, a fifth straight monthly increase, even as Hormuz risk keeps prices elevated. Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI held firm at 53.1 in July (from 53.3), with Kuwait's reading rebounding. The PIF, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, approved its 2026–2030 strategy, pivoting toward value creation with tourism, travel and entertainment as priority sectors under Vision 2030.

GLOBAL
The Hormuz standoff and a hawkish Fed repricing are now the two swing factors for global risk sentiment. Washington's new demands on Tehran have clouded any near-term reopening of the strait, keeping oil bid and inflation risk — and hence rate-hike odds — elevated into September's FOMC.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: 5th IMF EFF/RSF review due next month (~$1.2bn at stake) — wins: banks, FX reserves, sovereign risk; loses: energy consumers facing tariff conditionality.
• GCC: OPEC+ +188,000 bpd for August; PIF's 2026–2030 strategy backs tourism/entertainment — wins: oil-importing economies, Saudi non-oil diversification plays; loses: OPEC+ producers' per-barrel revenue.
• Global: Fed repricing toward a 25bp September hike (~55% odds) — wins: USD, fixed-income savers; loses: rate-sensitive equities, EM FX including the PKR.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 178,500 (deeper support 176,500) · pivot 179,847 (Tuesday's close) · resistance 181,017 (Tuesday's high), then 181,310. We read this as a geopolitical repricing, not a trend reversal — a close back above 181,000 reopens record territory; a break of 178,500 points to a deeper retracement. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
